methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective study with 109 patients and a sample size calculation based on published conversion rates. The use of STROBE guidelines, Clavien-Dindo complication classification, and appropriate statistical tests (ANOVA with Tukey post hoc, chi-square) is appropriate. The three BMI group comparison is a meaningful stratification. Key limitations include small Group A size (n=26), single-center design limiting generalizability, and retrospective data collection. Confounders such as body fat distribution, surgeon experience over time, and case complexity are not formally adjusted for.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The clinical relevance is direct: Class III obesity is common in EC patients and surgical decision-making is practically impacted. The finding of comparable complication rates but longer operative time and reduced bilateral SLN mapping in Class III obesity is immediately actionable for preoperative counseling and surgical planning. Single-center retrospective design and limited follow-up (3 months) limit the strength of conclusions about oncological completeness and long-term outcomes.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript explicitly references STROBE guidelines and includes a STROBE flowchart. Outcome definitions (SLN mapping failure, complications, feasibility) are clearly pre-specified with explicit caveats about the definition of feasibility. Clavien-Dindo classification is used consistently. The text notes a minor inconsistency in post hoc test reporting (p=0.002 in text vs p=0.026 in abstract for SLN mapping), suggesting minor inconsistency. No data repository is mentioned. Ethics committee approval and consent procedures are documented.

novelty_literature.justification: The study confirms existing literature showing that robotic surgery is safe in morbidly obese patients and that SLN detection rates are lower in this group. Similar findings have been reported by Lechartier et al., Papageorgiou et al., and the network meta-analysis by Ronsini et al. that are all cited in the manuscript. The specific focus on Class III (BMI≥40) rather than BMI>35 and the Italian ESGO-accredited center context add modest incremental value. No novel methodology, tool, or finding is introduced.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized and readable with a logical structure. Statistical results are clearly presented in tables. The limitations are appropriately acknowledged. Minor issues include a text-abstract inconsistency in SLN mapping p-values and a brief 'bias' section that would benefit from more formal confounder discussion. The discussion contextualizes findings appropriately within the existing literature and references the ongoing RObese trial.

key_strengths: Well-defined patient cohort with complete data from an ESGO-accredited center, using standardized SLN protocol and uniform robotic surgical approach across all groups
Pre-specified sample size calculation and clear definition of the primary outcome (surgical feasibility) with appropriate separation of hysterectomy completeness from nodal staging
Clinically relevant finding that bilateral SLN mapping fails nearly 4-fold more often in Class III obesity (OR 3.85), providing quantifiable risk for preoperative counseling
Reference to the ongoing RObese RCT appropriately contextualizes the study within evolving evidence
key_concerns: Group A has only n=26 patients, limiting statistical power for rare outcomes (intraoperative complications, laparotomy conversion) and reducing confidence in non-inferiority conclusions
Minor inconsistency between abstract (p=0.026 for SLN mapping) and results text (p=0.002 for lymphadenectomy rate) requires clarification before publication
3-month follow-up is insufficient to evaluate oncological outcomes (nodal staging adequacy, recurrence risk) which are critical for the clinical significance of reduced SLN success rates
Single-center design and lack of adjustment for surgical experience, case complexity, or body fat distribution limit generalizability to other settings
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competent single-center retrospective study confirming the safety of robotic surgery in Class III obese EC patients with a new quantifiable SLN mapping risk; suitable for Tier 3 with minor revisions addressing statistical inconsistencies and limitations of short follow-up.
